title: Design challenges
objective: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to follow the engineering design process: define a problem, list its constraints, compare ideas and build a first prototype.

sections.title: What engineers do
sections.text: Engineers solve problems by designing things, such as bridges, water filters, phones and roads. They follow a design process: a set of steps they can repeat until the solution works well.

sections.title: Define the problem
sections.text: Start by saying clearly what the problem is and who it is for. "Water bottles keep falling off our desks" is clearer than "make something cool". Then write the criteria: what a good solution must do, for example hold a 1 litre bottle without tipping over.

sections.title: Constraints
sections.text: Constraints are the limits you must work within, such as materials, money, time and size. In a class challenge you might only get 20 straws, some tape and 30 minutes. Real engineers have constraints too, like a solar lamp that must be cheap enough for families to buy.

sections.title: Ideas, then build
sections.text: Brainstorm many ideas and sketch them before choosing one. Pick the idea that best meets the criteria within the constraints. Then build a prototype, which is an early model you can test and improve.

examples.title: Example 1: Checking a constraint
examples.code:
straws_used = 18
straw_limit = 20
print("Within the limit:", straws_used <= straw_limit)

examples.title: Example 2: Staying within a budget
examples.code:
budget = 300
costs = [150, 80, 45]
left = budget - sum(costs)
print("Left to spend:", left)

check_questions.prompt: In a design challenge you may use only 20 straws and 1 metre of tape. What are these called?
check_questions.explanation: Limits on materials, money, time or size are constraints.

misconception.0: Criteria describe what the solution must do, not the limits you work within.
misconception.2: A prototype is an early model you build, not a limit.
misconception.3: Results come from testing, not from the rules of the challenge.

check_questions.prompt: What is the best first step in the engineering design process?
check_questions.explanation: You need to know exactly what problem you are solving before you plan or build anything.

misconception.0: Building before you understand the problem often wastes time and materials.
misconception.1: Expensive materials are not always better, and you may break a cost constraint.
misconception.3: You cannot test something you have not designed and built yet.

check_questions.prompt: Why do engineers come up with many ideas before choosing one?
options: More ideas give a better chance of finding one that meets the criteria
The first idea is always wrong
Having many ideas means you never need to test
check_questions.explanation: Comparing several ideas makes it more likely you find one that fits the criteria and the constraints.

misconception.1: Brainstorming is useful work, not a way to pass time.
misconception.2: The first idea can be good. Comparing ideas helps you check.
misconception.3: Every design still needs testing, however many ideas you had.

try_it.title: Try It Yourself
try_it.instructions: Change straws_used to 25 and run the code. Does the design still meet the constraint?
try_it.starter:
straws_used = 18
straw_limit = 20
print("Within the limit:", straws_used <= straw_limit)
